headline: Independent MP Helen Haines Discharged From Hospital After Accident
metaDescription: Independent Australian MP Helen Haines has been discharged from a Melbourne hospital four weeks after suffering injuries in an alleged car incident.
aiSummaryBullets: Independent MP Helen Haines left The Alfred hospital in Melbourne on Monday.
The discharge occurred four weeks after she was struck by a vehicle outside her electorate office.
Haines required a double leg amputation following the incident in regional Victoria.
aiContextParagraph: Independent Australian politician Helen Haines, representing the electorate of Indi, has been released from medical care following a significant incident occurring four weeks prior. The Member of Parliament was struck by a vehicle outside her office located in Wangaratta, regional Victoria. Following the collision, Haines was transported to The Alfred hospital in Melbourne, where she underwent a double leg amputation. The hospital officially confirmed her discharge on Monday, though no additional medical details were disclosed at that time. The incident has been described as an alleged attack involving a man who struck the parliamentarian with a car. Investigations regarding the event have been ongoing since the incident took place at her electorate office. As a representative for the Indi electorate, the situation has garnered attention regarding the safety of public figures working in regional areas of Australia.
